evidence.section_title: Barbara Liddle University of Sydney and Susan H. Spence
evidence.quote: Subjects were randomly assigned to one of three groups, namely Social Competence Training (SCT), Attention Placebo Control (APC) and No Treatment Control (NTC).

[page/3/Text/3] The present study differs from other published studies cited in combining both a follow-up assessment and a non-specific treatment control group which will make it possible to determine if any beneficial effects are specific to the treatment. It also used a combined cognitive—behavioural approach to therapy, as combined approaches have been found to be superior than either cognitive or behavioural methods alone with adult populations (Taylor and Marshall, 1977).

[/page/4/Text/6] The chosen subjects were randomly allocated to one of three treatment conditions, namely, social competence training (» = 11), attention placebo (n = 10) and waiting list control (» = 10).

[/page/8/Text/2] Social Competence Training (SCT). The SCT programme was designed to teach overt social skills, cognitive restructuring, and interpersonal problem solving skills which would be used in problematic social situations identified by the children in the groups. The content of the SCT was adapted from programmes outlined by Camp and Bash (1981), Spivack and Shure (1978), Rathjen and Foreyt (1980), Spence (1980) and techniques based on adult Cognitive Therapy (Beck, Rush, Shaw and Emery, 1979).

evidence.section_title: Barbara Liddle University of Sydney and Susan H. Spence
evidence.quote: Thirty-one children, aged 7 to 11 years, were selected on the basis of depressive symptomatology over a two week period, as assessed by self-report questionnaires and a diagnostic interview.

[/page/3/Text/8] This allowed conformity with DSM-III-R criteria for a Major Depressive Episode which state that symptoms must be of at least two weeks duration. Children exceeding a score of 40, which is recommended as [/page/4/Text/2] the score required for a child to be diagnosed as depressed (Poznanski, Mokros, Grossman and Freeman, 1985), were then selected as subjects.
[/page/4/Text/6] Parental permission was sought for inclusion in the therapy phase of the study for those children who were categorized as meeting the criteria for depression.

[/page/3/Text/7] All children whose parents consented (no parents refused permission) completed the Children's Depression Inventory {(CDI) Kovaks, 1985] on a class basis. The questionnaire was read out to younger children and those whose reading was poor. [/page/3/Text/8] To further validate the levels of depression experienced by the children identified by the CDI, each child exceeding the cut-off score was individually interviewed two weeks later using the Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (CDRS-R; Poznanski, Grossman, Buchsbaum, Banegas, Freeman and Gibbons, 1984).
